summary: At just 1.5 square miles, Home Gardens isn't technically a city at all — it's an unincorporated census-designated place in Riverside County, tucked between Corona and the city of Riverside, which means no city council, no municipal services of its own, and county governance handling everything from road maintenance to code enforcement. The terrain is flat Inland Empire valley floor, and with a density of 7,620 people per square mile packed into that tiny footprint, the landscape reads as tightly gridded residential blocks rather than sprawling suburbia. A median home value of roughly $499,000 against a median household income of $92,344 yields a price-to-income ratio around 5.4 — stretched but not impossible, and notably cheaper than coastal Southern California. Rent at $1,744 per month consumes about 23% of that median income, which is relatively manageable. The area functions almost entirely as a bedroom community; major employment centers in Corona, Riverside, and the warehouse-and-logistics corridor along the I-15 and SR-91 draw commuters outward, and those freeway corridors are notoriously congested during peak hours. With average highs around 76°F and nearly ten hours of daily sunshine year-round, summer heat regularly pushes past 100°F — air conditioning isn't optional. The 6.6% poverty rate sits well below national averages, but the area lacks a distinct commercial core or walkable retail district, making it a place defined more by proximity to everywhere else than by anything anchored within its own borders.
